hourly.summary: United fans are venting frustration after a disappointing 1-1 home draw against 10-man Tottenham, conceded via a stoppage-time Solanke header. Rashford's barren run continues (zero goal contributions since return), Mainoo looks lost in midfield, and Sesko's injury leaves the attack threadbare. Managerial carousel chatter (Howe, Nagelsmann, Amorim) dominates, with Howe's 'podcast vibe' and Nagelsmann's 'Ten Hag-esque communication issues' drawing scepticism. Carrick's interim stint earns mixed reviews — Rashford dropped, Baleba praised — but the mood is pure 'same old United'.

daily.summary: Sentiment plummeted from pre-match frustration (4/10) into full-blown crisis (2/10) after a 1-1 home draw with 10-man Tottenham extended United's worst start in 40 years. The day traced a sharp descent: early tension over Carrick's tactics and Rashford's form curdled into post-match meltdown, with 'Carrick OUT' chants, boos at Old Trafford, fans chanting 'we are fucking shit', and INEOS reportedly weighing the manager's future. The only consistent positives were academy graduates — Baleba's debut, Yoro's minutes, Mainoo's form, and the U18s' fight — highlighting a widening chasm between youth promise and senior collapse.

weekly.summary: The week began with fleeting schadenfreude over Manchester City's 115 charges but rapidly curdled into a sustained cycle of aggrieved grievance — fixated on INEOS ownership, institutional bias, and United's own injury crisis. A brief mid-week recovery fueled by the women's derby win and transfer optimism proved short-lived, as the period closed in grim resignation: toxic outrage at Zirkzee and the regime settling into gallows humor that masks a fanbase that has normalized mediocrity and a 13-year title drought.
